citation: Munns, R., & Tester, M. (2008). Mechanisms of salinity tolerance. Annual Review of Plant Biology, 59, 651–681. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.arplant.59.032607.092911
design: Review of physiological and molecular mechanisms of plant salinity tolerance
finding: Salinity constrains plant growth through osmotic and ionic effects, while tolerance depends on multiple physiological mechanisms.
use: Broad biological background and mechanism vocabulary.
boundary: This review does not establish the exact effect size for the classroom radish conditions.

citation: Munns, R., & Gilliham, M. (2015). Salinity tolerance of crops – what is the cost? New Phytologist, 208(3), 668–673. https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13519
design: Review focused on crop salinity effects and costs
finding: Soil salinity can reduce crop growth and yield, with plant responses and tolerance varying among species and conditions.
use: Supports the bounded background claim that salinity can constrain plant performance.
boundary: The review concerns crop salinity broadly; it is not a direct estimate for this radish seed batch.

citation: Toscano, S., Romano, D., Cafaro, V., & Patanè, C. (2025). Annual Garden Rocket and Radish as Microgreens: Seed Germination Response to Thermal and Salt Stress. Agronomy, 15(2), 361. https://doi.org/10.3390/agronomy15020361
design: Experimental study of temperature and NaCl-related water potential during rocket and radish germination
finding: Radish germination and early radicle growth varied with temperature and salinity-related water potential; radicle length declined under stronger salt stress conditions.
use: Species-relevant evidence that radish early growth is responsive to saline germination conditions.
boundary: Its temperatures, water-potential treatments, sample structure, and outcome procedures differ from this teaching exemplar.
